notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/avatar.guide.tsx and the AvatarGuide part of the shared src/AvatarGuides.tsx, lines 425–664 with its helpers GuideAvatar, AvatarCard and AvatarVisual) and from the Avatar lines of the shared docs/evidence/avatar-and-avatargroup.md, at 31f1c5e (“docs: add onboarding home page, component search, and favicon”, 29 September), the same files on main and docs-next. The AvatarGroup guide in the same file (AvatarGroupGuide, MixedAvatarGroup, AvatarGroupSpecimen, AvatarGroupCard) and the evidence's AvatarGroup, AmountInput and NoteInput lines are left out: AvatarGroup has no entry, and none of its sentences render on the Avatar page. The guide's Sources note and the evidence were checked on 23 September 2026 on jfs-components 0.1.60, so items citing them carry 2026-09-23 and 0.1.60 and the trace check flags them; the mirror has no 0.1.60 tag, so no GitHub compare to the installed build is possible. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). Every guide sentence quoted here was read against the installed Avatar.tsx and skeleton/Skeleton.tsx (read, not rendered), with token values through the package's own getVariableByName (lib/commonjs): Avatar Size L, M, S and XS resolve avatar/size to 42, 36, 29 and 14 px, and L is the collection's default, so an Avatar with no modes is 42 px; avatar/radius is 9999, the circle sentinel (borderRadius size / 2, Avatar.tsx 69–83); the monogram is centred (48–55) in avatar/label tokens (16/14/12/10 px at L/M/S/XS, weight 500, JioType Var, 74–80, 103–110) on avatar/background, which only Monogram gets (93); Image draws imageSource with resizeMode cover inside the same circle (281–306), and with no imageSource it draws the bundled 31595e70….png (22, 289), the same picture for every Avatar; style defaults to Image and monogram to “MS” (149–151). Loading: the installed Avatar reads loading ?? the SkeletonGroup's active (166–167) and returns a Skeleton kind other of the same width and height (216–226), whose radius token cornerRadius/defaultSkeleton is 9999 (a circle) on bg/defaultSkeleton, rgb(231, 231, 231). That matches the States copy used here (same size, neutral, token-backed circle). It contradicts the evidence's 0.1.60 line “in the checked web runtime a direct `loading={true}` outside an active `SkeletonGroup` renders no placeholder”: since then Avatar passes visible={loading === true} and Skeleton draws when visible even with no active group (Skeleton.tsx 134, 272–275). So the States description “Loading is a runtime state supplied through SkeletonGroup, not a style or size variant.” and the Sources line “Loading replaces Avatar content with a neutral, token-backed Skeleton inside an active SkeletonGroup.” now say less than the package: loading also works on its own. Neither sentence is quoted; the loading rule rests on the package's loading fact (its JSDoc), and the guide fix is in reviews/avatar.json. Accessibility: the installed source still does what the 0.1.60 Sources note and evidence say: accessibilityLabel is accepted on the type and discarded (154–157), the root View, or the Pressable when onPress is set, has role image and accessibilityLabel undefined (251–254, 268–271), and the inner Text and Image are hidden from accessibility (234–235, 302–303); the item keeps its 0.1.60 date and stays flagged until the guide is re-checked. The JSDoc's “If not provided, uses monogram or "User avatar"” (123) is not what the code does; that is a screen-reader name, so it is not counted as a Coin gap here and no bug is filed. Not recorded: onPress and disabled (the guide keeps Avatar non-interactive and documents neither), the pressed scale (0.98) and web focus border, Context2, Page type and the other mode collections the package says Avatar reads (Context2 AppBar only changes avatar/border/size to 3, with a transparent border colour; no Avatar guide sentence covers any of them), Color Mode (building rules), the Storybook story list (still the four stories the Sources note names, index.json last modified 17 October 2026), Figma's property names, and the playground. Anatomy: Circle and border is always present; Monogram content and Image content each appear only with their style. Content good keeps the guide's monograms MS and AK; there is no bad copy. avoidWhen keeps the Do & Don't's fallback case (the Image style with no imageSource for different people); the guide names no other component to use instead. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every Avatar and Card), and Avatar Size only where the guide shows a size other than the default (M in its In context, XS for the one-letter rule); the In context example lays out the guide's Card (variant slim, Card.Title and Card.SupportText) with HStack and VStack, which stand in for the guide's own CSS row; the image URI stands for the person's own photo. All components used have an entry in this pack. Left out of examples (three at most): the anatomy specimens, the size row, the loading specimens (SkeletonGroup has no entry), and the fallback Don't. Consistency with earlier entries that already use Avatar: brandchip examples 0–2 (AB for an Axis Bank account) and threadhero examples 0–2 (RV, VR for a person) use style Monogram with initials at the default size, which agrees with this entry. appbar example 1 sets no style and no imageSource, so it draws the bundled fallback image, which this entry's configuration and Do & Don't keep for previews; it also sets Color Mode, Context2 and Page type, which AppBar already passes to its slots (AppBar.tsx 169–170, cloneChildrenWithModes). rechargecard example 0 uses Monogram Avatars for app logos (JH, JS) and an overflow count (+2), which the Avatar guide doesn't cover: its summary is one person or account, and its content rule is initials. Those entries are not changed in this batch. Sorting (batch 11, two cross-check runs). Round 1 flagged /facts/props/4: its description said the root is a View, or a Pressable with onPress, both with role image, which the evidence doesn’t say (it is in the installed source); our misreading of the evidence, so the description now keeps to the evidence’s words. Round 1 also flagged /examples/0: it said M is the size the guide shows and called “Account owner” a name; the purpose now says M is what the guide’s In context card draws in its code (AvatarGuides.tsx: AvatarCard renders GuideAvatar, whose size defaults to M, lines 58, 160 and 555; its copy names no size) and calls Account owner a role. Rounds 1 and 2 flagged /configuration/7 (lost-context: loading true without a SkeletonGroup), resting on the 0.1.60 evidence; it is dismissed in reviews/avatar.json, because the installed Avatar draws the placeholder with loading alone (Avatar.tsx 167 and 216–226; Skeleton.tsx 134 and 272–275). The out-of-date loading sentences and the 0.1.60 check are the guide fix in reviews/avatar.json (human flag on the whole entry). Round 2’s notes, not flags: the cross-check suggests qualifying the package’s loading fact, which the installed source bears out; /examples/0’s M can’t be seen in the copy (it is in the guide’s code). Left: the two 0.1.60 trace-check flags (/facts/props/4 and /accessibility/0, both still true on dbe0e02 as read here) and the human flag. Ticket (coordinator, batch 11): no open ticket covered the Avatar guide, so the guide fix is the new Documentation ticket #533; the human flag points there.

evidenceFacts.name: accessibilityLabel
evidenceFacts.description: Accepted by the type but discarded: the implementation hides the inner image and text from accessibility and gives the pressable wrapper role image.
evidenceFacts.quote: The component type accepts `accessibilityLabel`, but the implementation discards it, hides inner image/text from accessibility, and renders the pressable wrapper with role `image`.
